question: Does odd Frobenius trace on the normalized cubic root curve tighten the arithmetic Q(t) cover-pool bound?
population: The six family presentations used by the frozen sixteen-fibre panel; omit MW16-05, which is not in that panel. Reuse the verified inversion for curve398.
inputs: Family A,B coefficient arrays and exact squarefree discriminant factors only. No generic or exceptional points, rank labels, Kummer classes or search results enter counting workers.
selection: In increasing order, take the first three odd primes at most 499 for which denominators are invertible, the discriminant factors preserve degree/multiplicity/coprimality, c4 stays coprime to the discriminant, infinity is good, and every I2 root-curve node stays ordinary. Do not select primes by the observed counts.
endpoint: Exact normalized root-curve counts and parity. An odd count, combined later with the independently certified generic Kummer dimension and reciprocal Frobenius polynomial, bounds rational Jacobian 2-torsion by 2g-2. The local I2 allowance adds at most one dimension to the Q(t) pool.
failure: Preserve UNKNOWN if fewer than three eligible primes exist or a worker exceeds its cap. No larger prime bound and no automatic retries. Even counts give no improved bound; they are not evidence of extra rational torsion.
